question: Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection of poems titled:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gitanjali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature for Gitanjali (Song Offerings), becoming the first Asian Nobel laureate (गीतांजलि के लिए 1913 का साहित्य नोबेल पुरस्कार — रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर)

 

• He was also the first non-European to receive the Nobel in Literature.

 

• The English prose translation of Gitanjali, introduced by W. B. Yeats, drew the attention of the Swedish Academy.

 

• Tagore was born in Calcutta on 7 May 1861 to Debendranath Tagore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tagore wrote the national anthem Jana Gana Mana, adopted officially in 1950.

 

• He also composed Amar Shonar Bangla, later Bangladesh's national anthem.

 

• Gora is a novel; Sonar Tari is a collection of poems published in 1894.

 

• He was awarded a knighthood in 1915.

 

• Gitanjali was first published in Bengali in 1910, and Tagore himself made the English prose version that Yeats prefaced in 1912.

 

NOTE

 

• Gora (Option 1): Gora is Tagore's well-known novel on identity and nationalism, but it is a work of fiction and not the poetry collection that earned the Nobel Prize in 1913.

 

• Chitra (Option 2): Chitra is a verse play based on the Mahabharata story of Chitrangada; it is a separate work of Tagore and was not the book honoured by the Nobel committee.

 

• Sonar Tari (Option 4): Sonar Tari is an early poetry collection of 1894 and, although admired, it was Gitanjali in its English translation that the Swedish Academy recognised in 1913.

question: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in 1919 in protest against the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tagore gave up the knighthood conferred in 1915 as a protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of April 1919 (जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड के विरोध में नाइटहुड का त्याग)

 

• In his letter to Viceroy Chelmsford he said that the badges of honour looked ridiculous in the context of the humiliation of his countrymen.

 

• General Dyer's firing at Amritsar on 13 April 1919 killed hundreds of unarmed people gathered on Baisakhi.

 

• The renunciation made Tagore a symbol of moral resistance to colonial violence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hunter Committee of 1919 inquired into the Punjab disturbances.

 

• Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal in 1920 over the Khilafat and Punjab wrongs.

 

• Tagore had earlier led the Rakhi Bandhan procession during the Bengal partition.

 

• Tagore held the title of Sir for only four years, from 1915 to 1919.

 

NOTE

 

• Partition of Bengal (Option 2): The Partition of Bengal occurred in 1905, fourteen years before the renunciation; Tagore opposed it through the Rakhi Bandhan festival, but the knighthood was not yet given then.

 

• Rowlatt Act (Option 3): The Rowlatt Act of March 1919 was the immediate cause of the protests in Punjab, but Tagore specifically renounced his title in response to the massacre that followed.

 

• Simon Commission (Option 4): The Simon Commission arrived in 1928, nine years after Tagore returned his knighthood, so it could not have been the cause of the 1919 renunciation.

question: Rabindranath Tagore founded Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan, West Bengal in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1921.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Visva-Bharati was founded by Tagore at Santiniketan in 1921 as a university with an international outlook (विश्वभारती विश्वविद्यालय की स्थापना — 1921)

 

• It grew from the school he had begun in 1901 and aimed at a blend of Indian and world cultures through open-air learning.

 

• It became a central university in 1951 under an Act of Parliament.

 

• Tagore's educational vision stressed creativity and harmony with nature.

 

• The university was created to bring together the best of Eastern and Western learning, and Tagore directed classes to be held beneath trees.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The motto of Visva-Bharati is Yatra Visvam Bhavatyekanidam.

 

• Gurudev Tagore used the Nobel prize money to strengthen the institution.

 

• The Sriniketan rural reconstruction centre was added in 1922.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru's daughter Indira studied at Santiniketan briefly.

 

• The Sriniketan wing, started in 1922 under Leonard Elmhirst, extended the idea of rural reconstruction to nearby villages.

 

NOTE

 

• 1901 (Option 1): The year 1901 saw the beginning of Tagore's school at Santiniketan, which was the precursor, but the university called Visva-Bharati was established twenty years later.

 

• 1913 (Option 2): In 1913 Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature; this was a literary honour and not the date of founding the university.

 

• 1935 (Option 4): By 1935 Visva-Bharati had already been functioning for fourteen years, so this is far too late for its establishment.

question:
Consider the following statements about Rabindranath Tagore:

1. He was born in Calcutta on 7 May 1861.

2. His father was Debendranath Tagore.

3. He founded Visva-Bharati at Wardha.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Tagore was born in Calcutta (Bengal Presidency) on 7 May 1861 into the Jorasanko Tagore family (7 मई 1861 को कलकत्ता में जन्म — रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: his father was Debendranath Tagore, a leader of the Brahmo Samaj and known as Maharshi.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Visva-Bharati was founded in 1921 at Santiniketan in West Bengal, not at Wardha, which is in Maharashtra and linked with Gandhi.

 

• Tagore was a poet, writer, philosopher, composer and educationist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tagore's grandfather Dwarkanath Tagore was a pioneering industrialist.

 

• Wardha hosted Gandhi's Sevagram ashram from 1936.

 

• Tagore was the first Asian Nobel laureate (1913).

 

• He composed over two thousand songs known as Rabindra Sangeet.

 

• Tagore's elder brother Satyendranath became the first Indian member of the Indian Civil Service, a fact often linked to the Jorasanko family.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): This option relies on statement 3, which is false because Visva-Bharati lies at Santiniketan in Bengal; it also leaves out statement 1 on his Calcutta birth in 1861.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Statement 3 misplaces Visva-Bharati at Wardha, and the pairing leaves out statement 2, whereas Debendranath Tagore was indeed his father.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Accepting all three fails since statement 3 is wrong; the university was founded in Santiniketan, whereas Wardha is Gandhi's later centre in Maharashtra.

question: Who founded the Indian Home Rule Society and India House in London in 1905?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shyamji Krishna Varma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the Indian Home Rule Society in London in 1905 and set up India House as a base for Indian students (लंदन में इंडिया हाउस की स्थापना — श्यामजी कृष्ण वर्मा)

 

• India House, at Highgate, offered scholarships and lodging to Indian students and became a crucial meeting place for revolutionaries.

 

• His journal The Indian Sociologist spread the ideas of Indian self-rule among students abroad.

 

• V. D. Savarkar and Madan Lal Dhingra were among the young men connected with the house.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madan Lal Dhingra assassinated Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909.

 

• Varma left London in 1907 under official pressure, which ended the early phase of the house.

 

• The India House is sometimes called the first overseas centre of Indian revolutionary activity.

 

• Varma had been a student of Sanskrit at Oxford and a lawyer.

 

NOTE

 

• Madame Bhikaji Cama (Option 1): Madame Cama was an associate of the society and India House but not its founder; she is remembered as the one who unfurled an Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907.

 

• Rash Behari Bose (Option 2): Rash Behari Bose worked in India and later Japan, where he founded the Indian Independence League in 1942; he had no part in the London society.

 

• Lala Har Dayal (Option 4): Lala Har Dayal helped create the Ghadar Party in California in 1913, a different overseas organisation, and he did not found India House in London.

question: Who was the first person to hoist an Indian flag on foreign soil, at the International Socialist Conference in Stuttgart, Germany, in 1907?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madame Bhikaji Cama.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madame Bhikaji Cama hoisted the Indian flag on 22 August 1907 at the International Socialist Conference, Stuttgart, with 'Vande Mataram' written on it (स्टटगार्ट में पहली बार विदेशी धरती पर भारतीय ध्वज — मैडम भीकाजी कामा)

 

• She is known as the Mother of Indian Revolution for her work in Paris, London and the United States.

 

• She was linked with the Indian Home Rule Society and India House in London.

 

• Her flag carried green, saffron and red bands, with eight lotuses standing for the provinces of British India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Born in Bombay in 1861, she belonged to a Parsi family.

 

• She published the journal Bande Mataram from Paris.

 

• She returned to India in 1935 and died in Bombay in 1936.

 

• The flag she raised is displayed at the Maratha and Kesari Library in Pune.

 

• The Stuttgart congress was a meeting of the Second International, and Cama used the platform to appeal for human rights and freedom for India.

 

NOTE

 

• Annie Besant (Option 1): Annie Besant was an Indian-based theosophist and Home Rule leader who became Congress president in 1917; she did not raise the Stuttgart flag in 1907.

 

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 2): Sarojini Naidu was a poet and Congress leader who presided in 1925; she was not at Stuttgart and is not credited with the first foreign flag hoisting.

 

• Aruna Asaf Ali (Option 3): Aruna Asaf Ali raised the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank in Bombay in 1942 during Quit India, an act inside India and thirty-five years after Stuttgart.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Shyamji Krishna Varma established India House in London as a hostel for Indian students.

2. Madame Bhikaji Cama is called the 'Mother of Indian Revolution'.

3. India House was established in Paris.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Varma set up India House in London in 1905 as a hostel and meeting place for Indian students (इंडिया हाउस — लंदन में छात्रावास)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Bhikaji Cama's long exile and her propaganda in Europe and America won her the title Mother of Indian Revolution.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: India House stood in London (Highgate), not Paris, although Cama's own journal was printed in Paris and Varma later moved there.

 

• The two leaders worked together through the Indian Home Rule Society.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Varma's society had the slogan that the Indian must be free to determine his own destiny.

 

• Another London group, the Free India Society, was led by Savarkar from 1906.

 

• Cama's Paris flat served as a centre for exiles.

 

• Varma later shifted to Paris and then Geneva, while Cama stayed on in Paris for many years.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): This option wrongly adds statement 3 about Paris and omits statement 1; India House was situated in London and run as a student hostel by Shyamji Krishna Varma.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): The pairing drops statement 2, which is true, and keeps the false claim that India House was a Paris institution, when it was based in the British capital.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Statement 3 spoils the set because the hostel was in London; the Paris link relates only to Cama's later residence and publication activity.

question:
Assertion (A): India House in London became a crucial meeting place for Indian revolutionaries.

Reason (R): It was a hostel for Indian students established by Shyamji Krishna Varma.

Which one of the following is correct?
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: India House at London served as a centre where young Indian nationalists met and planned (इंडिया हाउस — क्रांतिकारियों का केंद्र)

 

• Reason R is true: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded it in 1905 as a hostel for Indian students studying in England.

 

• R explains A because the hostel brought together many young radicals under one roof, giving them lodging, books and a platform.

 

• The Indian Sociologist, circulated from this base, encouraged them to think of political freedom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Savarkar joined India House in 1906 while studying law.

 

• Pressure from Scotland Yard forced Varma to leave London in 1907.

 

• The house was shut after the murder of Curzon Wyllie in 1909.

 

• The Indian Home Rule Society was formed in February 1905.

 

• The Indian Sociologist, which Varma edited, carried Herbert Spencer's maxim that resistance to aggression is not simply justifiable but imperative.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): The two statements are connected rather than independent: the student hostel is exactly why India House attracted young radicals, so R is the cause of A.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): Reason R is accurate because Varma really did create the house as a hostel for Indian students, so the claim that R is false cannot be accepted.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): Assertion A is accurate, since India House was indeed a crucial meeting place for revolutionaries, so describing A as false is not correct.

question: The Indian Independence League was founded in Tokyo in 1942 by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rash Behari Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rash Behari Bose founded the Indian Independence League in Tokyo in 1942 to organise Indians in East Asia (टोक्यो में इंडियन इंडिपेंडेंस लीग — रास बिहारी बोस)

 

• He was an important figure of the Ghadar movement and helped form the Azad Hind Fauz (Indian National Army) from prisoners of war.

 

• He was honoured by Japan with the Order of the Rising Sun.

 

• In 1943 he handed over the leadership of the league and the INA to Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rash Behari Bose threw a bomb at Viceroy Hardinge at Delhi in December 1912.

 

• He fled to Japan in 1915 and settled there.

 

• The Tokyo conference of March 1942 led to the league's creation.

 

• He died in Tokyo in January 1945.

 

• After 1943 the league became the political wing of the Provisional Government of Azad Hind, headquartered at Singapore and later Rangoon.

 

NOTE

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose (Option 1): Subhas Chandra Bose took over the league's leadership in 1943 and then formed the Provisional Government of Free India; he did not found it in Tokyo in 1942.

 

• Mohan Singh (Option 3): Mohan Singh organised the first INA from Indian prisoners of war in Malaya in 1942, but he was an army officer and not the founder of the league at Tokyo.

 

• Taraknath Das (Option 4): Taraknath Das was a revolutionary based in the United States and associated with the Ghadar movement, and he did not set up the league in Japan.

question:
Consider the following statements about Rash Behari Bose:

1. He was a prominent figure in the Ghadar movement.

2. He played a part in the formation of the Azad Hind Fauz.

3. He founded the Indian Home Rule Society in London.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Rash Behari Bose took part in the plans of the Ghadar movement of 1915 for an armed uprising (गदर आंदोलन में भूमिका — रास बिहारी बोस)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he helped in the formation of the Azad Hind Fauz in East Asia during the Second World War, before Subhas Bose took charge.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Indian Home Rule Society was founded in London by Shyamji Krishna Varma in 1905; Bose operated from India and Japan.

 

• Bose's own organisation was the Indian Independence League of 1942.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ghadar Party was formed in 1913 in San Francisco by Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna.

 

• The planned February 1915 Ghadar rebellion was betrayed and crushed.

 

• He married a Japanese woman and took Japanese citizenship.

 

• The Hardinge bomb case took place at Chandni Chowk.

 

• Bose's 1915 escape to Japan under the name P. N. Tagore, a relative of the poet, helped him evade British detectives.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 is wrong, and this option leaves out statement 1; Shyamji Krishna Varma, not Rash Behari Bose, established the Indian Home Rule Society in London.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): This pairing omits the true statement 2 on the Azad Hind Fauz and includes the false claim about a London society that was in reality Varma's work.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): All three cannot be correct because statement 3 credits Bose with a London-based society founded in 1905 by Varma, which was unconnected with Bose.

question: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement, was popularly known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Frontier Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a Pashtun leader from the North-West Frontier Province, was called Frontier Gandhi or Badshah Khan (सीमांत गांधी — खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान)

 

• He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) movement, whose members wore red shirts and followed Gandhi's non-violence.

 

• He strongly opposed the partition of India and felt betrayed when the Congress accepted it in 1947.

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987, the first non-Indian citizen to receive it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khudai Khidmatgar was started in 1929.

 

• The Qissa Khwani Bazaar firing at Peshawar occurred in April 1930.

 

• He lived long in Pakistan and was imprisoned there for his political views.

 

• He died in Peshawar in 1988 and was buried at Jalalabad, Afghanistan.

 

• Ghaffar Khan's Khudai Khidmatgars gave the Congress a strong base in the Frontier, and the Congress formed a ministry there after the 1937 elections.

 

NOTE

 

• Lion of Punjab (Option 1): Lion of Punjab is the epithet of Lala Lajpat Rai, a Punjab leader who died in 1928, and it has no connection with the Pashtun leader of the Frontier.

 

• Deshbandhu (Option 2): Deshbandhu, meaning Friend of the Nation, was the title of Chittaranjan Das of Bengal, founder leader of the Swaraj Party, not of the Khudai Khidmatgar founder.

 

• Iron Man of India (Option 3): Iron Man of India refers to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Home Minister, and does not describe Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the Pashtun non-violence leader.

question:
Consider the following statements about Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan:

1. He was a Pashtun leader from the North-West Frontier Province.

2. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987.

3. He supported the partition of India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Ghaffar Khan was a Pashtun leader of the North-West Frontier Province (पख्तून नेता — उत्तर-पश्चिम सीमा प्रांत)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he was given the Bharat Ratna in 1987, in recognition of his role in the freedom movement.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: he strongly opposed partition, famously telling the Congress leaders that they had thrown the Pashtuns to the wolves.

 

• His loyalty to Gandhian non-violence made him the Frontier Gandhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• He rejected the Muslim League's two-nation theory.

 

• The NWFP referendum of July 1947 offered only a choice between India and Pakistan, which the Khudai Khidmatgars boycotted.

 

• His brother Dr Khan Sahib led the Congress ministry in the province.

 

• Ghaffar Khan's autobiography is titled My Life and Struggle.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): This option includes the wrong statement 3, since Ghaffar Khan opposed partition, and it fails to count statement 1 about his Pashtun identity from the frontier region.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): The combination leaves out the Bharat Ratna of 1987 and backs partition, which is the reverse of Ghaffar Khan's stand against dividing the country.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Statement 3 makes the full set untenable, because the Frontier Gandhi opposed partition even as the Congress consented to it in 1947.

question: Who hoisted the national flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay during the Quit India Movement in 1942?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aruna Asaf Ali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 9 August 1942, the day after the Quit India resolution (गोवालिया टैंक पर तिरंगा फहराया — अरुणा आसफ अली)

 

• The Congress leaders were arrested early on 9 August, and she stepped forward to lead the flag ceremony at the ground.

 

• She later worked underground, edited the journal Inquilab with Ram Manohar Lohia and became the first Mayor of Delhi.

 

• She received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1997.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Quit India was launched at Gowalia Tank on 8 August 1942, after Gandhi's call of 'Do or Die'.

 

• Usha Mehta ran the Congress Radio, a secret station, in Bombay in 1942.

 

• Gowalia Tank is now known as August Kranti Maidan.

 

• She was married to Asaf Ali, a Congress lawyer.

 

NOTE

 

• Sucheta Kripalani (Option 1): Sucheta Kripalani worked in the underground movement of 1942 and later became Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, yet the flag-hoisting at Gowalia Tank is credited to another woman leader.

 

• Kasturba Gandhi (Option 3): Kasturba Gandhi had been arrested with her husband and died in detention at Aga Khan Palace in February 1944, so she did not hoist the flag at Bombay in 1942.

 

• Usha Mehta (Option 4): Usha Mehta is remembered for running the secret Congress Radio in 1942, a different contribution to Quit India than the Gowalia Tank flag-hoisting.

question: Which woman revolutionary was shot dead while hoisting the national flag at a police station in Assam during the Quit India Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanaklata Barua.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanaklata Barua, a teenager from Assam, was shot dead in September 1942 while leading a procession to hoist the national flag at Gohpur police station (असम की शहीद कनकलता बरुआ)

 

• She was part of the Mrityu Bahini, a death squad of young volunteers of the Quit India Movement.

 

• She was about seventeen years old and carried the flag forward even after the police fired on the procession.

 

• She is regarded as one of the best-known women martyrs of 1942.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gohpur lies in Sonitpur (then Darrang) district of Assam.

 

• Matangini Hazra was shot at Tamluk in Bengal during the same movement.

 

• Bhogeswari Phukanani was killed at Barhampur in Nagaon district.

 

• The Gohpur martyrs are remembered every September in Assam.

 

• Kanaklata's martyrdom is often grouped with that of Matangini Hazra at Tamluk, whose last words were Vande Mataram during the same movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Matangini Hazra (Option 1): Matangini Hazra, an elderly Gandhian, was killed at Tamluk in Midnapore, Bengal, while carrying the flag in 1942; the Assam martyr who hoisted the flag at a police station was someone else.

 

• Bhogeswari Phukanani (Option 2): Bhogeswari Phukanani, an elderly woman from Nagaon district, died after being struck during a clash with police in 1942, and she is a different martyr from the teenage flag-bearer of Gohpur.

 

• Pritilata Waddedar (Option 3): Pritilata Waddedar was a revolutionary of Chittagong who died in 1932 after an armed attack on a club, an act belonging to the Chittagong group and not to Quit India in Assam.

question: Baji Raut, regarded as the youngest martyr of the freedom struggle, was shot dead in 1938 for refusing to ferry British police across which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baji Raut, a 12-year-old boatman from Dhenkanal, Odisha, was shot on 11 October 1938 for refusing to ferry the police across the Brahmani river (सबसे कम उम्र का शहीद बाजी राउत — ब्राह्मणी नदी)

 

• The police were pursuing freedom fighters of the Dhenkanal praja mandal agitation against the local ruler and wanted to cross at Nilakanthapur ghat.

 

• He sounded the alarm to the villagers and refused the order, and the police opened fire.

 

• He is remembered as the youngest martyr of India's freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dhenkanal movement was led by Sarangadhar Das and the Prajamandal.

 

• Odisha's princely states saw popular agitations in 1938-39 against feudal rulers.

 

• The Brahmani flows through Odisha into the Bay of Bengal near Dhamra.

 

• A memorial at Nilakanthapur honours Baji Raut and the others killed that day.

 

• Odisha's princely states, such as Dhenkanal, Talcher and Nilgiri, saw Prajamandal agitations demanding responsible government in this period.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahanadi (Option 2): The Mahanadi is Odisha's longest river and flows near Cuttack, but the incident of 1938 happened at the Brahmani crossing at Nilakanthapur in Dhenkanal district.

 

• Godavari (Option 3): The Godavari is a peninsular river flowing through Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, far from Dhenkanal, and has no link with the boatman's refusal of 1938.

 

• Hooghly (Option 4): The Hooghly is a distributary of the Ganga in West Bengal on which Calcutta stands; Baji Raut's ferry was in Odisha and not on that river.

question: Which revolutionary, executed by the British in 1931 at the age of 23 in connection with the Lahore Conspiracy Case, is remembered as 'Shaheed-e-Azam'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhagat Singh was hanged on 23 March 1931 at the age of 23 in the Lahore Conspiracy Case and is honoured as Shaheed-e-Azam, the Great Martyr (शहीद-ए-आजम भगत सिंह)

 

• He was convicted for the killing of the police officer Saunders, an act carried out to avenge the death of Lajpat Rai.

 

• In April 1929 he and Batukeshwar Dutt threw harmless bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly, shouting 'Inquilab Zindabad'.

 

• He was a leader of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) and the Naujawan Bharat Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged with him.

 

• Bhagat Singh was born in 1907 at Banga in Lyallpur district.

 

• His 116-day hunger strike in jail drew national attention.

 

• Gandhi's inability to stop the hanging caused anger at the Karachi session of 1931.

 

• Rajguru, Sukhdev and Bhagat Singh are remembered every 23 March as Martyrs' Day, and their memorial stands at Hussainiwala in Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Chandrashekhar Azad (Option 1): Chandrashekhar Azad died in a police encounter at Alfred Park, Allahabad, in February 1931, before Bhagat Singh's hanging, and he was never tried or hanged in the Lahore case.

 

• Khudiram Bose (Option 2): Khudiram Bose was hanged in 1908 at about 18 for the Muzaffarpur bomb attack, a Bengal case from the Swadeshi era and not the Lahore Conspiracy Case of 1931.

 

• Ashfaqulla Khan (Option 4): Ashfaqulla Khan was hanged in December 1927 for the Kakori train robbery of 1925, a different conspiracy tried in Lucknow and not the Lahore case.

question: Which of the following leader–organisation pairs is NOT correctly matched?
option_2: Gopal Krishna Gokhale – Servants of India Society
option_3: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan – Khudai Khidmatgar
option_4: Rash Behari Bose – Indian Independence League
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shyamji Krishna Varma – Ghadar Party.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in the United States by Punjabi migrants, with Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna as leaders, while Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the Indian Home Rule Society in London (घदर पार्टी — हरदयाल और भकना, वर्मा नहीं)

 

• Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 at Pune, so that pair is correct.

 

• Ghaffar Khan founded the Khudai Khidmatgar, the Red Shirt movement of the Frontier, which is also a correct pairing.

 

• Rash Behari Bose set up the Indian Independence League in Tokyo in 1942, again a correct pairing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Varma's other creation besides the Home Rule Society was India House at London.

 

• The Ghadar newspaper was started in 1913 at San Francisco.

 

• Rash Behari Bose also worked with the Ghadar rebels in 1915.

 

• Ghaffar Khan's movement dates from 1929.

 

• The Ghadar Party's weekly Ghadar was published in Urdu, Punjabi and other languages from San Francisco to circulate the call for revolt among Indians abroad.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale – Servants of India Society (Option 2): This pairing is accurate, since Gokhale established the Servants of India Society in 1905, so it cannot be the incorrect match that the question asks for.

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan – Khudai Khidmatgar (Option 3): The pairing is accurate because Ghaffar Khan founded the Khudai Khidmatgar, known as Servants of God, among the Pashtuns of the North-West Frontier Province.

 

• Rash Behari Bose – Indian Independence League (Option 4): This is a correct match, as Rash Behari Bose created the Indian Independence League in Tokyo in 1942 to rally Indians living in East and Southeast Asia.

question: Which of the following leader–title pairs is NOT correctly matched?
option_1: Gopal Krishna Gokhale – Socrates of Maharashtra
option_3: Madame Bhikaji Cama – Mother of Indian Revolution
option_4: Annie Besant – Mother of Indian Revolution
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Besant – Mother of Indian Revolution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annie Besant was a theosophist and Home Rule leader and the first woman Congress president, but the title Mother of Indian Revolution belongs to Madame Cama (मदर ऑफ इंडियन रेवोल्यूशन — भीकाजी कामा)

 

• Gokhale was called the Socrates of Maharashtra, a correct pairing.

 

• Chittaranjan Das was honoured with the title Deshbandhu, meaning Friend of the Nation, which is correct.

 

• Madame Cama, associated with the Indian Home Rule Society and the Stuttgart flag, rightly carries the title of Mother of Indian Revolution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Das founded the Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru in 1923.

 

• Besant's papers were Commonweal and New India.

 

• Gokhale's mentor was Ranade.

 

• Cama unfurled the flag in 1907 at Stuttgart.

 

• Besant is remembered instead for Theosophy, the Home Rule League and the daily New India, while the Mother of Indian Revolution title stays with Cama.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale – Socrates of Maharashtra (Option 1): This pairing is right, because Gokhale's moderation and rational public work led to his being called the Socrates of Maharashtra, so he is not the mismatch in the list.

 

• Chittaranjan Das – Deshbandhu (Option 2): This is a correct match, since Chittaranjan Das of Calcutta was honoured as Deshbandhu for his sacrifice of a lucrative legal practice and his leadership of the Swaraj Party.

 

• Madame Bhikaji Cama – Mother of Indian Revolution (Option 3): The pair is correct because Madame Cama, who campaigned from Paris and Stuttgart, is the leader known as the Mother of Indian Revolution, so she is not the wrong pairing.

question: The Swaraj Party was formed in 1923 by Motilal Nehru and which other leader, honoured with the title 'Deshbandhu'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chittaranjan Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 with Motilal Nehru, and he was honoured with the title Deshbandhu, 'Friend of the Nation' (स्वराज पार्टी के संस्थापक — देशबंधु चित्तरंजन दास)

 

• Das, born in Calcutta in 1870, was a leading barrister who gave up his practice to join the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• The Swaraj Party opposed the Congress's boycott of councils and aimed at entering the legislatures to obstruct the government from within.

 

• As the president of the Gaya session in 1922 he lost the debate on council entry, which led him to form the new party.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Das defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case in 1909.

 

• He was the first Mayor of Calcutta in 1924.

 

• The party's other leaders included Vithalbhai Patel and Madan Mohan Malaviya's allies in the Assembly.

 

• He died in Darjeeling in June 1925.

 

• Das also founded the newspaper Forward, later renamed Liberty, and his Swaraj Party won many seats in the 1923 council elections in Bengal and the Central Provinces.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 2): Lajpat Rai remained associated with the Hindu Mahasabha and an independent stand in the Assembly and was not a founder of the Swaraj Party; the Deshbandhu title is not his.

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 3): Madan Mohan Malaviya founded Banaras Hindu University and was a Congress and Hindu Mahasabha leader; he was never called Deshbandhu and did not co-found the Swaraj Party.

 

• Vithalbhai Patel (Option 4): Vithalbhai Patel served the Swarajists as a member and later became the first Indian Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly, but he was not the leader with the Deshbandhu title.

question:
Match the leaders in Column A with their associated works or institutions in Column B.

Column A: (a) Bal Gangadhar Tilak (b) Lala Lajpat Rai (c) Gopal Krishna Gokhale (d) Annie Besant

Column B: (i) Servants of India Society (ii) Kesari (iii) Punjab National Bank (iv) New India
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tilak – Kesari: Tilak ran the Marathi newspaper Kesari from Pune (तिलक — केसरी; लाजपत राय — पंजाब नेशनल बैंक; गोखले — भारत सेवक समाज; बेसेंट — न्यू इंडिया)

 

• Lajpat Rai – Punjab National Bank: he co-founded the Punjab National Bank at Lahore in 1894.

 

• Gokhale – Servants of India Society: he founded this body in 1905 to train workers for the nation.

 

• Besant – New India: she published the daily New India at Madras along with the weekly Commonweal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak's English weekly was Mahratta.

 

• Lajpat Rai also edited the Arya Gazette.

 

• Gokhale's society was based in Pune.

 

• New India was bought by Besant in 1914 and turned into a daily.

 

• The Punjab National Bank, one of the oldest surviving Indian banks, was among the first to be started purely with Indian capital.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 1): This match swaps the first two: Kesari was Tilak's Marathi paper, and the Punjab National Bank was co-founded by Lajpat Rai, so a-iii and b-ii are mistaken.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv (Option 2): Here Lajpat Rai is paired with the Servants of India Society and Gokhale with the bank; the society was Gokhale's and the bank was Lajpat Rai's, so b-i and c-iii are wrong.

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii (Option 3): This one pairs Tilak with New India and Besant with Kesari; the daily New India was Besant's and Kesari was Tilak's, so a-iv and d-ii are incorrect.

question:
Match the leaders in Column A with the items in Column B.

Column A: (a) Surendranath Banerjee (b) Shyamji Krishna Varma (c) Madame Bhikaji Cama (d) Rash Behari Bose

Column B: (i) Indian Independence League (ii) Indian National Conference (iii) India House (iv) Flag hoisting at Stuttgart
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Banerjee – Indian National Conference: he organised the Indian National Conference of 1883, which merged with the Congress in 1886 (बनर्जी — नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस; वर्मा — इंडिया हाउस; कामा — स्टटगार्ट; बोस — इंडियन इंडिपेंडेंस लीग)

 

• Varma – India House: Shyamji Krishna Varma set up India House in London in 1905 as a student hostel.

 

• Cama – flag hoisting at Stuttgart: Madame Cama unfurled the flag in 1907 at the International Socialist Conference.

 

• Rash Behari Bose – Indian Independence League: he founded the League in Tokyo in 1942.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian National Conference met at Calcutta in December 1883.

 

• India House was in Highgate, north London.

 

• The Stuttgart meeting was held on 22 August 1907.

 

• The Indian Independence League later passed under Subhas Bose's leadership.

 

• Banerjee's Indian National Conference had met before the Congress, and Rash Behari Bose's league overlaps with Subhas Bose's later Indian National Army campaign.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i (Option 1): This option gives India House to Banerjee and the National Conference to Varma, reversing the pairs; Varma built the hostel in London and Banerjee organised the conference.

 

• a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i (Option 2): In this version Varma is linked to the Stuttgart flag and Cama to India House; the flag was raised by Cama, while India House was founded by Varma.

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii (Option 4): This one gives the League to Banerjee and the National Conference to Bose, which is wrong because Bose headed the League in 1942, while Banerjee held the 1883 conference.

question:
Match the works in Column A with their authors in Column B.

Column A: (a) Arctic Home of the Vedas (b) Unhappy India (c) Gitanjali (d) Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

Column B: (i) Dadabhai Naoroji (ii) Rabindranath Tagore (iii) Bal Gangadhar Tilak (iv) Lala Lajpat Rai
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arctic Home of the Vedas – Tilak: Tilak argued in this 1903 book that the Aryans came from the Arctic (आर्कटिक होम ऑफ द वेदाज — तिलक; अनहैप्पी इंडिया — लाजपत राय; गीतांजलि — टैगोर; पॉवर्टी एंड अन-ब्रिटिश रूल — नौरोजी)

 

• Unhappy India – Lajpat Rai: written in 1928, it rebutted the book Mother India.

 

• Gitanjali – Tagore: this poetry collection won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature.

 

• Poverty and Un-British Rule in India – Naoroji: the book of 1901 set out the Drain of Wealth theory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak also wrote the Gita Rahasya during his imprisonment at Mandalay.

 

• Lajpat Rai also wrote The Story of My Deportation.

 

• Tagore's English Gitanjali had a preface by W. B. Yeats.

 

• Naoroji's drain calculations were also discussed before the Welby Commission.

 

• Tilak, Lajpat Rai, Tagore and Naoroji each combined writing with public action, which is why their books are often used in the quiz of notable works.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i (Option 1): This option swaps the authors of the first two works; the Arctic theory was advanced by Tilak and Unhappy India was authored by Lajpat Rai, so a-iv and b-iii are wrong.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii (Option 2): Here Gitanjali is given to Naoroji and the economic critique to Tagore, which reverses the real authorship: Gitanjali is Tagore's and the drain book is Naoroji's.

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii (Option 3): This combination assigns Poverty and Un-British Rule to Tilak and the Arctic work to Naoroji, whereas Naoroji wrote the former and Tilak the latter, so a-i and d-iii fail.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

(a) Bhagat Singh was executed

(b) Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British House of Commons

(c) Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature

(d) Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society
solution_text:
The correct answer is b, d, c, a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Naoroji's election (b) to the House of Commons took place in 1892 (क्रम: नौरोजी 1892, गोखले 1905, टैगोर 1913, भगत सिंह 1931)

 

• The Servants of India Society (d) was founded by Gokhale in 1905.

 

• Tagore's Nobel Prize (c) was awarded for Gitanjali in 1913.

 

• Bhagat Singh's execution (a) occurred on 23 March 1931, the latest event of the four.

 

• Chronology therefore runs Naoroji, Servants of India Society, Tagore's Nobel Prize and finally Bhagat Singh, covering four decades from the 1890s to 1931.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Naoroji election was in the constituency of Finsbury Central.

 

• The year 1905 also saw the Partition of Bengal.

 

• Between 1913 and 1931 fall Tagore's renunciation of knighthood and the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• Karachi Congress followed the hanging in March 1931.

 

• Between Naoroji's election and Bhagat Singh's execution lie 39 years, a span that covers Swadeshi, Home Rule, Non-Cooperation and the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

NOTE

 

• d, b, c, a (Option 1): This puts the 1905 society ahead of Naoroji's election in 1892, which reverses the order; Naoroji entered Parliament thirteen years before the Servants of India Society was founded.

 

• b, c, d, a (Option 3): This puts the Nobel Prize of 1913 before the 1905 founding of the Servants of India Society, which is out of order, since the society is nearly eight years older.

 

• b, d, a, c (Option 4): This places Bhagat Singh's execution of 1931 ahead of the Nobel Prize of 1913, which cannot be right, because Tagore won the prize eighteen years before the hanging.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

(a) Annie Besant became President of the Congress

(b) Tagore renounced his knighthood

(c) Tagore founded Visva-Bharati as a university

(d) Tilak launched the Home Rule League
solution_text:
The correct answer is d, a, b, c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tilak's Home Rule League (d) was launched in 1916, before Besant's league of the same year (क्रम: 1916 होम रूल, 1917 बेसेंट, 1919 नाइटहुड त्याग, 1921 विश्वभारती)

 

• Besant's presidency (a) of the Congress came at Calcutta in 1917.

 

• Tagore's renunciation (b) of knighthood followed the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919.

 

• Visva-Bharati (c) as a university was founded at Santiniketan in 1921.

 

• The correct order thus follows the sequence of Tilak's league, Besant's presidency, the Jallianwala Bagh protest of Tagore and the university at Santiniketan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak launched his league in April 1916 at Belgaum.

 

• The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916.

 

• The Rowlatt Act of March 1919 preceded the massacre of April 1919.

 

• Tagore's school at Santiniketan began in 1901.

 

• The decade from 1916 to 1921 saw Home Rule, the Lucknow Pact, the Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh, the Khilafat issue and the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

NOTE

 

• a, d, b, c (Option 2): This order puts Besant's 1917 presidency ahead of Tilak's 1916 league, which is wrong because the Home Rule movement had begun the year before she presided at Calcutta.

 

• d, b, a, c (Option 3): This puts Besant's 1917 presidency after Tagore's 1919 renunciation, whereas she presided in 1917, two years before the Jallianwala Bagh massacre prompted the renunciation.

 

• d, a, c, b (Option 4): Visva-Bharati was formed in 1921, after the knighthood was renounced in 1919, so placing it before Tagore's renunciation contradicts the sequence of events.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

(a) Puducherry was transferred from French control to India

(b) Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank

(c) Goa was freed from Portuguese rule

(d) Baji Raut was shot at the Brahmani river
solution_text:
The correct answer is d, b, a, c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baji Raut's death (d) occurred on 11 October 1938 in Odisha (क्रम: 1938 बाजी राउत, 1942 अरुणा आसफ अली, 1954 पुदुचेरी, 1961 गोवा)

 

• Aruna Asaf Ali's flag-hoisting (b) took place on 9 August 1942 during Quit India.

 

• Puducherry's transfer (a) came in 1954.

 

• Goa's liberation (c) through Operation Vijay followed in December 1961.

 

• The sequence runs from the 1938 Dhenkanal incident through Quit India in 1942, then the French cession of 1954 and finally the Portuguese colony's end in 1961.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Quit India began on 8 August 1942 at Bombay.

 

• Independence in 1947 falls between the second and third events.

 

• The de jure transfer of Puducherry was recognised in 1962.

 

• Sardar Patel died in December 1950, before either territory merged.

 

• The events span the late colonial era and the first decade after Independence, covering the final phase of Quit India and the integration of foreign enclaves.

 

NOTE

 

• b, d, a, c (Option 1): This order puts the 1942 flag-hoisting ahead of Baji Raut's death in 1938, which cannot be right because the Dhenkanal incident preceded the Quit India Movement by four years.

 

• d, a, b, c (Option 2): This puts the 1954 Puducherry transfer ahead of the 1942 Gowalia Tank event, which is wrong because Aruna Asaf Ali's act came during the freedom struggle, before independence.

 

• d, b, c, a (Option 4): This puts Goa's 1961 liberation ahead of the 1954 Puducherry transfer, a reversal of the actual order, since the French enclaves merged seven years before Portuguese Goa.
